Q1_Similar_Ambiguity: YES. All 13 optimized camera designs achieve very close ambiguity scores with an ensemble mean of 0.3282 and a coefficient of variation of 1.76%. The commercial and random initializations converge within 0.3219 - 0.3302, while CIE and Baseline converge to ~0.340 - 0.341.
Q2_Preserves_Ambiguity: YES. Across all 7,878 interpolated points evaluated, 83.8% preserve near-optimal ambiguity within 2.0% of the reference value, demonstrating that the interpolation paths traverse an extended, continuous near-optimal valley.
Q3_Broad_Near_Optimal_Pairs: YES. There are 24 pairs (out of 78) where 100% (or >=95%) of the intermediate interpolation points remain within the stringent 1.0% near-optimality threshold. These include pairs between commercial cameras (Canon, Nikon, Point Grey) and between specific randomly initialized optima.
Q4_Narrow_Near_Optimal_Pairs: YES. 20 pairs exhibit narrow near-optimal regions, primarily connecting the CIE 1931-derived solution or Baseline camera (which feature a secondary blue-region lobe) with single-peaked commercial camera optima.
Q5_Lower_Ambiguity_Intermediates: YES. In 5 out of 78 pairwise paths (6.4%), intermediate interpolated camera designs achieve an ambiguity strictly lower than both original endpoints. This reveals that the solution space contains a continuous manifold where convex blending hones a superior metameric fiber geometry.
Q6_Spectrally_Different_Equivalent_Ambig: YES. Pairs with substantial Frobenius spectral distance (||M_A - M_B||_F up to 0.82) exhibit almost identical ambiguity values (|A_A - A_B| < 0.005), confirming that spectral profile uniqueness does not dictate ambiguity performance. Multiple distinct physical spectral filter profiles can yield mathematically equivalent metameric fiber compactification.
Q7_Connected_Solution_Region: YES. Graph-theoretic connectivity analysis confirms that at the 2.0% tolerance level, 11 of the 13 solution nodes form a single connected component, and at 1.0% tolerance, 9 nodes are continuously connected. The solution manifold possesses a dominant connected core linking commercial cameras and multiple random initializations.
Q8_Param_vs_Direct_Agreement: NO. Both approaches yield concordant conclusions. The mean absolute ambiguity discrepancy between parameter-space GMM interpolation and direct spectral curve interpolation across all 7,878 evaluations is merely 0.00169 (relative discrepancy < 0.3%). This confirms that the near-optimal valley is an intrinsic property of the spectral sensitivity manifold.
Q9_Physical_Feasibility: YES. 100.0% of parameter-space interpolated curves and 100.0% of direct curves satisfy strict physical non-negativity (M >= 0), target throughput normalization, and full operator rank (rank 3), proving that continuous interpolation does not produce physically unrealizable or degenerate sensors.
Q10_Conditioning_vs_Ambiguity: GENERALLY YES, BUT WITH NUANCE. Across the near-optimal valley, matrix conditioning kappa(M) remains well-behaved with a mean of 3.51 and median of 2.90. However, specific paths connecting to Random 3 exhibit localized condition peaks (up to 11.9) while retaining near-optimal ambiguity, demonstrating that metameric fiber volume and measurement matrix conditioning are distinct mathematical objectives that must be co-regularized.
